components.css: .ds-slip{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) 240px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.14);border-radius:14px;overflow:hidden;background:rgba(46,36,66,0.62);color:#f6f6f7;} .ds-adv{display:grid;gap:4px;padding:18px 22px;} .ds-l{font-family:Inter,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;font-size:13px;color:#cbbfd0;} .ds-payee{font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;font-size:15px;color:#ece6f0;} .ds-amt{font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;font-weight:600;font-size:30px;line-height:1.15;letter-spacing:-.01em;} .ds-foil{position:relative;display:grid;align-content:center;justify-items:start;gap:8px;padding:18px 22px;border-left:2px dashed rgba(255,255,255,0.28);background:rgba(233,182,90,0.1);} .ds-foil::before,.ds-foil::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:-9px;width:16px;height:16px;border-radius:50%;background:#1c1e3e;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.14);} .ds-foil::before{top:-9px;} .ds-foil::after{bottom:-9px;} .ds-stamp{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;padding:5px 11px 5px 8px;border:2px solid #e9b65a;border-radius:6px;color:#e9b65a;font-family:"IBM Plex Mono",ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;font-weight:600;font-size:20px;line-height:1;letter-spacing:.04em;transform:rotate(-3deg);animation:ds-land .38s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) both;} .ds-note{font-family:Inter,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;font-size:14px;color:#e6e0ea;} @keyframes ds-land{from{opacity:0;transform:scale(1.7) rotate(-11deg);filter:blur(2px);}to{opacity:1;transform:scale(1) rotate(-3deg);filter:none;}} @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-stamp{animation:none;}}

narrative.overview:
Albashi lives in the paperwork a Nigerian payment leaves behind. On the public page that is a phone's lock screen at dusk over Lagos: frosted notification cards from the sender ALBASHI, set like bank credit alerts. On the owner's desk it is the same dusk carried indoors: a book of pay-advice slips, each torn along a dashed perforation, whose counterfoil is stamped PAID when the pay-run contract's event is read, or DECLINED and struck when nobody signed it. Both surfaces are one world: violet-to-navy night, frosted translucent panels, one warm gold that means money arrived, and monospaced figures you could check against the chain.

The system is dark, quiet and exact. Density is moderate on the desk (laptop-first ledger, 16px body) and theatrical only in the public first viewport, where the live rate is set at lock-screen clock scale. Decoration is almost absent; character comes from the artefacts (alert, slip, perforation, stamp) and from the strict split between words (Inter) and records (IBM Plex Mono).

The two surfaces do not share one token file. The proof page defines its colours on `:root` in `globals.css` (plus a calmer set scoped to the below-the-fold reading sections); the desk redefines its own set under `.desk` in `desk.css`, borrowing only the gold, night, navy, declined grey, ink and font variables from `:root`. The frontmatter records the values both actually use; where a value belongs to one surface only, the prose says so.
keyCharacteristics: Dusk violet into navy ground; never a white or neutral-grey canvas.
Frosted, translucent panels with hairline white edges; depth by blur and tone, not shadow.
Gold is the only accent, and it means a credit or the action that leads to one.
Declined is grey, struck through, and always spelled out in words.
Every figure, address, hash and alert in IBM Plex Mono; every sentence in Inter.

rules.name: The Gold Means Money Rule
rules.body: Gold appears only where a credit landed, a check passed, or on the one action that moves money forward (and, on the desk, the keyboard focus that leads to it). Never gold for decoration, headings or a second "brand" highlight.

rules.name: The Words Before Colour Rule
rules.body: A state is never colour alone. Declined is grey plus a strike plus the word DECLINED and the contract's reason; a warning is amber plus the sentence that explains it.

rules.name: The No Daylight Rule
rules.body: Every surface sits on the dusk ground. There is no light theme and no white panel.

rules.name: The Typed Record Rule
rules.body: Every figure, address, hash, block number, time stamp and alert line is set in IBM Plex Mono; every sentence, label and button is set in Inter. Never a naira amount in Inter outside the rate display.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Figures line up. The desk sets `tabular-nums` on its root; the proof page relies on Plex Mono's fixed widths for the same effect.

rules.name: The Frost Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: A panel is lifted by translucency and a hairline edge, never by an outer drop shadow.

dos: Do set every figure, address, hash, time and alert line in IBM Plex Mono and every sentence in Inter.
Do keep gold (#e9b65a) for credits, passed checks, PAID stamps and the single money-moving primary action.
Do show a refusal on the page: declined frost, grey, a strike, the word DECLINED and the contract's own reason.
Do put the source and read time next to every live value ("Textile FX quote, read 10:26 WAT").
Do lift panels with translucency and a white hairline edge over the dusk ground.
Do let only the stamp land; respect reduced motion.
Do shorten addresses to `0x1234…abcd` on narrow screens rather than letting them wrap through a slip.
donts: Don't introduce a light theme, white panels or a neutral grey canvas.
Don't use gold as a decorative highlight, a heading colour or a second brand tint.
Don't show a state by colour alone; warn-amber and declined-grey always travel with words.
Don't add drop shadows to panels or cards.
Don't replace the slip book with a KPI row over a generic transactions table.
Don't add a second animation vocabulary (slides, bounces, staggered reveals) beside the stamp.
